legend: ✅ built in, or in an official package of the same project (named) · ⚠️ partial, opt-in, with a caveat, or through a third-party package (named) · ❌ not built in · 🔜 planned by the maintainers, no code yet · — does not apply. Every cell of the alternatives was decided by reading the source of the latest published package and its official docs in October 2026, not its README; the syncom column is this repository.

transport.detail: The client ships an SSE-based `HttpTransport`, but the 1.x server only accepts WebSockets (on `/`). Its SSE `/message` routes are commented out in the legacy server.

webrtc.text: sync always goes through the server

partial.text: per-query sync, filtered by read permissions

resume.text: per-query checkpoint: server timestamp + cached ids
resume.source: @triplit/client@1.0.50 src/sync-engine.ts:693-748 (QueryState from latest_server_timestamp); @triplit/server-core@1.0.52 dist/sync-connection.js bufferEntityData (checkpoint diff), :225
resume.detail: There is no op log: on reconnect the server re-runs each query and sends the entities changed since the checkpoint, plus the ids that have left the result.

bootstrap.text: current query results, no history replay

conflicts.text: attribute patches; the last to reach the server wins
conflicts.note: The FAQ still describes per-attribute HLC timestamps from 0.x. In 1.x the server stamps each incoming batch with its own clock when it arrives, so an edit made offline hours ago overwrites newer values when it finally syncs.
conflicts.source: @triplit/db@1.1.10 src/server-entity-store.ts:13-19 (server clock.next() per batch), src/entity-metadata-store.ts (one timestamp per entity), src/entity-data-store.ts:196 applyChange; @triplit/server-core@1.0.52 dist/sync-connection.js:272; client CHANGES message carries no timestamp (client src/@triplit/types/sync.ts:106); docs faq.mdx:47 (outdated)

offline.text: durable outbox, optimistic, rebased on server data
offline.source: @triplit/client@1.0.50 src/sync-engine.ts:1178-1200 (failed locked buffer merged with pending writes); https://github.com/aspen-cloud/triplit/blob/main/packages/docs/src/pages/v1-migration.mdx:332; offline-mode.mdx
offline.detail: When the server rejects a batch, the whole batch stays in the outbox and is re-sent with every later write until the app clears it (`clearPendingChangesForEntity`/`…ForAll`). The docs warn that sync can get blocked.

serverAuth.text: server re-checks schema and permissions; can reject

signing.text: JWT per connection, not per change

atRest.source: grep encrypt|cipher|subtle over @triplit/db src, @triplit/client src, server dists: none (docs mention only JWT algorithms)

access.detail: Rules are not enforced on the client, and attribute-level rules are 'not yet supported' according to the docs.

purge.detail: This works only because 1.x keeps no history. The server keeps only a per-entity timestamp after a delete.

history.source: @triplit/db@1.1.10 src/entity-data-store.ts, src/entity-metadata-store.ts (latest entity + one timestamp per entity)

hooks.detail: The 0.x `addTrigger` and server webhooks were not ported to 1.x: the webhooks code is marked `@ts-nocheck` and its wiring is commented out.

observability.source: https://github.com/aspen-cloud/triplit/blob/main/packages/docs/src/pages/client/debugging.mdx; @triplit/server@1.1.8 dist/server.js:9-24 (SENTRY_DSN); no OpenTelemetry in any package

errors.source: @triplit/db@1.1.10 src/errors.ts:21-60 (31 subclasses); @triplit/client@1.0.50 src/sync-engine.ts:1155-1169 (switch on error.name, TriplitError.fromJson)
errors.detail: There are no error codes, and server errors arrive as a plain `TriplitError` carrying the subclass `name`, so `instanceof` fails. Branch on `name` instead.

server.text: Instant server + Postgres; Docker self-host or Cloud

schema.detail: Schema is optional: without it (or an `attrs` permission lock-down) `transact` creates new attributes on the fly.
